_comment: AgentContextPack index (design-spec 2.10). Each `areas` entry feeds one generated <state_dir>/contextpacks/<name>.context.md: `name` (the area; slugified into the pack filename), `folio` (the canonical entry-point doc for the area), `binding_docs` (authoritative contracts to read first), `source_roots` (key files/dirs; existence-checked at generation, missing ones flagged), `do_not_create` (existing systems an agent must not duplicate), `gates` (currently active expansion conditions), `verification` (commands to run before pushing). The generator also accepts a manifest snapshot ({"subsystems": [...]}) instead of this file.

areas.name: gameplay-simulation
do_not_create: a second spider motor — one fixed-step motor owns gravity, forward drive, and velocity limits
a second web constraint or a parallel rope implementation
a collision resolver outside CollisionPolicy — exactly one authoritative outcome per contact (GDD 13.2)
a global gameplay Manager autoload (GDD 19 forbids it; tests/test_runner.gd fails on any autoload)
a second source of simulation truth — SimulationWorld owns authoritative fixed-step state
an input poll inside simulation — simulation consumes buffered InputCommand values only
gates: PHASE 0 NOT STARTED. This area is empty by design; the bootstrap deliberately implemented no swing physics.

Phase 0 exit gate (GDD 23): attach/release predictable across supported frame rates; release preserves momentum; Reel-In useful without being mandatory; most test deaths correctly attributable by the player; one named physics preset approved as the baseline.
The core physics prototype must be approved before progression, monetization, missions, multiple spiders, or large content sets are built (GDD 1).

areas.name: run-application-orchestration
do_not_create: a second run lifecycle owner — RunStateMachine owns run transitions
a chunk spawner inside DifficultyDirector — the director selects, WorldStream owns spawned instances
a second settlement path — ScoreSettlement creates exactly one idempotent RunSettlement per run
a reward grant outside ProgressionService
a direct persistence write — SaveRepository (adapters) exclusively owns persistent writes
a parallel effect timer — EffectState owns power-up activation, refresh, and expiry
gates: PHASE 0 NOT STARTED. Empty by design.
Seeded chunk selection and the difficulty director are Phase 1, not Phase 0.
Run settlement, Silk, and progression are Phase 2. Phase 2 exit gate: economy grants cannot duplicate; progress survives app suspension and migration; upgrades do not affect standard records.

areas.name: godot-adapters
do_not_create: a second input path — InputRouter converts touch/UI into buffered commands and never mutates simulation
a second persistence writer — SaveRepository is the exclusive owner of persistent writes
a telemetry path that writes gameplay state; telemetry is read-only with respect to truth
a dependency on game/presentation/ — adapters and presentation are equal-rank peers
input action definitions outside project.godot's [input] section
gates: Input action names exist as definitions (web_action, reel_in, pause, restart_run, toggle_debug); no consumer is wired yet.
Touch bindings arrive with the Phase 0 input router, through the buffered-command seam — not a raw action poll.
Save, telemetry, and platform adapters are Phase 2.

areas.name: presentation
do_not_create: any write to authoritative simulation state from presentation
a reward, currency, record, or unlock grant from a UI node
a physics-driving visual web — the visual web follows authoritative endpoints (GDD 17.2)
a dependency on game/adapters/ — equal-rank peers
a second HUD root or a competing camera controller
gates: Bootstrap placeholder only: swing_lab.tscn renders the Phase 0 title and one runtime-facts line. No spider, no web, no camera follow.
Phase 0 adds the camera with speed-dependent look-ahead (spider held in the left third, GDD 4.2) and the diagnostic overlays from GDD 22.1.
Production art is Phase 2 (release-quality first biome). Avoid Spider-Man / superhero visual similarity (GDD 17.1).

areas.name: content
do_not_create: a spider variant that forks the player controller — spiders are data profiles (GDD 19.4)
a power-up that patches collision callbacks — effects use definitions and policy hooks
an obstacle chunk that modifies the director — chunks use validated metadata and sockets
content referenced by scene name or display text instead of a stable ID (GDD 19.3)
a spider that is a strict upgrade over Classic (GDD 14)
an upgrade granting starting Silk per run — a removed exploit (GDD 15.1)
gates: EMPTY BY DESIGN. Phase 0 uses a graybox debug course, not authored content.
Phase 1 adds three static obstacle chunks and one moving-hazard family. Every chunk must declare the full GDD 9.1 envelope and pass route validation.
Phase 1 exit gate: no observed unavoidable deaths in fixed-seed testing; every chunk valid for its declared speed/state range; every required route completable by the unupgraded Classic spider.
No Git LFS until real large binary assets justify it.

areas.name: build-release-infrastructure
do_not_create: a second host verification entry point — python3 tools/verify.py is the only one
a call to bootstrap.py check from tools/verify.py — the Substrate workflow runs its own check and this would recurse
a hand edit to substrate-gate.yml, auto-merge-enabler.yml, or branch-sweep.yml — kit-owned, regenerated by adopt/upgrade; change substrate.config.json instead
an unpinned `uses:` reference in a host-owned workflow — full commit SHA plus a tag comment, resolved from upstream and never invented
a production keystore, signing secret, store credential, or release/upload workflow
a CodeQL workflow — GDScript is not meaningfully covered by the standard language matrix
an engine version that disagrees with .godot-version
gates: Required merge checks: substrate-gate and game-quality.
android-debug is intentionally NOT a required check: it depends on external SDK downloads, so requiring it would turn a third-party outage into a merge block.
Production Android signing, Google Play publishing, and iOS signing are all deliberately absent and each is an owner-controlled step (ADR 0003).
No production credential, key, token, signing material, or store integration may be committed.
